title: India Replaces Education Secretary Amid NEET Protests in Sweeping Bureaucratic Reshuffle
excerpt: The Centre reshuffled 13 secretary-level posts across ministries, swapping out the higher education secretary as student demonstrations over NEET irregularities intensify.
body:
• The Centre carried out 13 secretary-level appointments on Thursday, replacing education secretary Vineet Joshi with Naresh Pal Gangwar amid continuing NEET paper leak protests.
  • Gangwar, a 1994-batch IAS officer from the Rajasthan cadre with an engineering background from IIT Delhi, takes over the Department of Higher Education.
  • T K Anil Kumar, a 1996-batch Karnataka cadre officer, was appointed secretary of School Education and Literacy.
  • The reshuffle extended well beyond education, with new appointments at Housing, Labour, Mines, the NHRC, and the National Commission for Minorities.

India's central government executed a sweeping bureaucratic reshuffle on Thursday, appointing 13 new secretaries across ministries in what amounts to one of the most extensive administrative overhauls in recent months. The most politically charged move: replacing Vineet Joshi as secretary of the Department of Higher Education, a change that comes as the government faces sustained pressure over alleged irregularities in the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test.

New Guard in the Education Ministry

Naresh Pal Gangwar, a 1994-batch IAS officer of the Rajasthan cadre, will take over as secretary of Higher Education. Gangwar brings a technical background to the role — he holds a BTech in Electronics and Communication from the University of Roorkee and an MTech in Communication from IIT Delhi, along with an MA in Economics from the University of Rajasthan. He was previously serving as secretary in the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying.

Joshi, a 1992-batch officer of the Manipur cadre, has been moved to the Ministry of Panchayati Raj. The government order issued by the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet offered no explanation for the change, but the timing is unmistakable.

"New Guard in the Education Ministry Naresh Pal Gangwar, a 1994-batch IAS officer of the Rajasthan cadre, will take over as secretary of Higher Education."

T K Anil Kumar, a 1996-batch IAS officer of the Karnataka cadre who had been serving as additional secretary in the Ministry of Rural Development, was separately appointed secretary of the Department of School Education and Literacy.

The NEET Shadow

The reshuffle unfolds against a backdrop of mounting public anger over the NEET examination. Students and civil society groups, including the Campaign for Judicial Reform and Peoples, have staged sustained demonstrations demanding accountability for alleged paper leaks and irregularities in the medical entrance exam. The protests have spread across multiple cities, with demonstrators calling for systemic reforms to India's high-stakes examination system.

While the government has not explicitly linked the education ministry changes to NEET, the optics of replacing the higher education secretary during active protests speak for themselves.

Reshuffle Reaches Far Beyond Education

The administrative overhaul touched nearly every corner of the government. Among the significant moves:

Katikithala Srinivas was transferred from Housing and Urban Affairs to head the Ministry of Development of the North Eastern Region. Piyush Goyal, the former secretary at the Ministry of Mines, was appointed secretary general of the National Human Rights Commission. Keshav Chandra takes over at Mines.

D. Thara moves to the Department of Capital Development under Housing and Urban Affairs. Chandra Bhushan Kumar was appointed at Labour and Employment, Satendra Singh at Urban Development, and Suchindra Misra at the National Commission for Minorities.

Sushil Kumar Lohani has been posted as Officer on Special Duty in the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying, filling the vacancy left by Gangwar's move to education.

In-Situ Upgrades Signal Continuity

The ACC also approved in-situ upgradations to Special Secretary rank for four officers who will continue in their current postings: Mritunjay Kumar Narayan (Registrar General of India), Santosh Kumar Yadav (Chairman, National Highways Authority of India), Rajeev Singh Thakur (Adviser, NITI Aayog), and Dilip Kumar (Director General of Training, Skill Development Ministry).

What It Means for NRI Students and the Diaspora

For the Indian diaspora, the NEET controversy carries direct implications. NRI-quota admissions to Indian medical colleges are governed by the same examination framework now under scrutiny, and families abroad who have invested heavily in their children's medical education prospects are watching the reform demands closely. Whether the new leadership at the education ministry signals substantive policy changes or merely a personnel rotation will become clear in the weeks ahead.
